model_annotation: The plot displays the performance or values of five different methods—FT, MEMIT, IKE, ROME, and an unnamed black line—across a logarithmic x-axis ranging from approximately 10⁻¹ to 10³, labeled as “-1”, “-2”, and “-3” (likely representing powers of 10, i.e., 10⁻¹, 10⁻², 10⁻³). The y-axis is linear and unlabeled, with gridlines and tick marks at regular intervals, though specific numerical values are not provided. Each method is represented by a distinct line with a unique color and marker: FT is blue with downward-pointing triangles, MEMIT is purple with circles, IKE is red with upward-pointing triangles, ROME is green with squares, and the unnamed line is black with solid circles. The green line (ROME) shows the highest values and a steep upward trend, starting at a moderate y-value and increasing significantly across the x-axis. The purple (MEMIT) and brown (unlabeled) lines begin at similar low values and rise steadily, with the brown line slightly surpassing MEMIT at the higher x-values. The red (IKE) and blue (FT) lines start at lower values and show gradual increases, with IKE consistently above FT. The black line remains the lowest throughout, increasing only slightly. All lines exhibit an upward trend, with ROME showing the most pronounced growth.
